dedupe_keys.name: ebro delta lagoon restoration and sediment management delta lagoon and ebro admiclim

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes two LIFE projects in the Ebro delta, Catalonia, Spain, where river regulation, subsidence and sea level rise (projected at 0.53 to 0.73 m by 2100) drive erosion, and storm Gloria in 2020 flooded 30 square kilometres with seawater. DELTA-LAGOON (2011-2014) reconnected the Alfacada lagoon directly to the river, reopened salt marshes split by dikes, turned rice fields back into lagoon and an old aquaculture site back into salt marsh, creating 62 hectares of habitat, for about 3.05 million euros. EBRO-ADMICLIM (2014-2018) tested injecting sediment from the Tarragona water purification plant into the irrigation network and sediment from dammed reservoirs into the lower river, optimised constructed wetlands and developed sediment transport guidelines and a model with the University of Córdoba, for about 2.26 million euros; its Climate Action Plan was adopted by the Catalan Office on Climate Change. The page, first published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the ICGC project page. Caveats: benefits were not valued in money, administrative disputes delayed some work, and the river basin authority did not support sediment reuse. It illustrates nature-based sea level rise hazard reduction and climate adaptation of a delta; related records are the Camargue saltworks and Lower Danube Green Corridor case studies.
name: Ebro delta lagoon restoration and sediment management (DELTA-LAGOON and EBRO-ADMICLIM)
outcomes: 62 ha of lagoon and marsh habitat were restored and sediment reuse was tested, leading to a planned sediment by-pass at the Riba-roja reservoir and an adopted Climate Action Plan.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the LIFE DELTA-LAGOON and EBRO-ADMICLIM projects
